saints.name: Sts. Felix and Adauctus
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: A Roman priest and an unknown bystander who joined him in confessing Christ unto death…
biography: Felix was a priest of Rome, martyred about the year 303 in the Great Persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that, condemned for refusing to sacrifice to the gods, he was led out to execution, and that a stranger in the crowd, moved by his constancy, stepped forward and openly declared himself a Christian.

The nameless man was seized and beheaded together with Felix; and because his name was never known, the faithful called him Adauctus, Latin for 'the added one' — added to Felix in martyrdom. The two have been honoured in one memory ever since, and are named in the most ancient sacramentaries and martyrologies.

They were buried in the catacomb of Commodilla on the Via Ostiensis, near the basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls, where Pope Damasus honoured them with an inscription and a church rose over their graves. Their relics were afterward carried north: some to the abbey of Eschau in Alsace about 850, others to St. Stephen's Cathedral in Vienna in 1361.
saints.knownFor: A martyrdom shared by a priest and an unnamed convert.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 30 August
